## How it works

- [statement] Hyperliquid documents order-book market liquidation followed by a vault backstop if book liquidation fails. Seuma's event study separately measures book-hitting and off-book forced flow. This supports separating liquidation-event intensity from the forced flow that actually consumes book liquidity. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-11-09) — https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.03616
- [statement] In Seuma's structural branching model, offspring mean equals price impact per forced dollar multiplied by forced notional per unit relative price move. This is a mechanistic branching ratio; it is distinct from the flow-based INAR/Hawkes estimator fitted to forced-sell counts. The paper does not establish either as a universal pre-cascade alarm. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2608.03616 · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters
- [statement] For the studied October 2025 Hyperliquid event, Seuma reports that the structural branching ratio remained subcritical, while the flow-based estimate fell through nucleation. These are attributed case-study findings from one research group, not independent replications or evidence that severe cascades require near-critical endogenous feedback. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2608.03616 · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Separate book-hitting forced flow from backstop transfers when constructing cascade-risk features. Garcia Seuma reports that off-book backstop absorption suppresses measured branching; Hyperliquid’s primary documentation describes order-book liquidation and a separate liquidator-vault backstop. This supports a venue-mechanism distinction, not a transferable numeric threshold. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2608.03616 · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters · also: https://hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/liquidations
- [statement] Across the seven BTC-perpetual cascades studied in Seuma's early-warning paper, no single variable supplies an event-invariant warning. Taker-flow variance compression survives as a population-level precursor but is too weak for a per-event alarm. The companion branching paper belongs to the same author's research program and adds no independent origin. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27070 · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.03616
- [statement] Do not treat open interest or aggressor flow as direct liquidation-arrival measurements. Garcia Seuma’s early-warning study explicitly uses these as consequences of forced liquidation because intraday liquidation microstructure is unavailable in its dataset. An intensity model fitted to such proxies estimates a different observable. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27070 · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters
- [statement] Lim's published journal abstract reports a Hyperliquid panel including SOL in which quoted spreads recovered while inside-quote depth remained impaired after the studied cascade. The author concludes that spread-only metrics understate post-event liquidity impairment. This supports checking depth as well as spread before lifting a proposed cascade-risk abstention state; it does not validate a specific reopening threshold. (low confidence) — https://journals.lincoln.ac.nz/index.php/JFDA/article/view/1395 · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters
- [statement] Treat multi-event, out-of-sample and placebo testing as prerequisites for a proposed liquidation-risk abstention filter. Garcia Seuma reports that a clean single-event early-warning pattern reverses out of sample and explicitly disclaims showing that a particular quoting rule would have helped. The cited evidence does not establish positive net trading value for abstention. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27070 · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters
- [statement] Seuma explicitly cautions that the calm-market level of the INAR/Hawkes estimate reflects mechanical clustering. Individual calm-baseline windows can exceed unity through small-sample behavior. A high fitted count-based branching level alone therefore cannot be interpreted as a demonstrated approach to criticality. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2608.03616 · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] A liquidation cascade is a feedback mechanism: forced closure of leveraged longs can depress prices and trigger further closures. This mechanism should motivate a stress filter, rather than be treated as proof of profitable directional prediction. (medium confidence) — https://www.allium.so/blog/how-a-liquidation-cascade-wipes-out-traders-in-minutes/ · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27070
- [statement] Cao and Gang report multivariate Hawkes clustering for Ethereum lending liquidations across Aave V3, Compound V3 and Morpho. They explicitly interpret cross-excitation as directional predictive dependence rather than identified structural causation; this adjacent lending evidence does not establish a perpetual-market cascade filter. (low confidence) — https://www.researchgate.net/publication/403263179_DeFi_Liquidations_Cluster_Across_Protocols_in_a_Multivariate_Hawkes_Framework · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters
- [statement] In Garcia Seuma’s crypto-perpetual case study, an INAR/Hawkes estimator based on forced-sell counts falls through cascade nucleation. Its calm-market level is mechanically inflated, so the author interprets the trajectory rather than the absolute level. A raw fitted branching threshold therefore needs measurement controls before it can serve as an abstention rule. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2608.03616 · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters
- [statement] For the historical Binance analysis, Seuma explicitly treats open interest and aggressor flow as proxies for the liquidation state rather than direct intraday liquidation measurements. The companion study can use a directly observed fill log only for its single in-flight case study. Proxy-derived warnings and measured liquidation-event intensity should therefore retain separate labels. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27070 · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.03616
- [statement] Methodological proposal, not a validated trading rule: evaluate a liquidation-risk abstention filter with causal features, unseen cascade episodes, ordinary-market placebos, and observable depth alongside spread. Measure whether the filter distinguishes adverse conditions before the decision rather than merely describing the crash. The cited studies motivate these checks but do not establish a profitable filter or a calibrated abstention threshold. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27070 · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters · also: https://arxiv.org/html/2608.03616, https://journals.lincoln.ac.nz/index.php/JFDA/article/view/1395

## Facts and statements

- [statement] For background, Heusser models Bitcoin trade-arrival intensity as history-dependent, with a baseline rate, event-triggered excitation and exponential decay. This is trade-arrival evidence, not an estimated perpetual-liquidation hazard or a SOL/Jupiter calibration. (low confidence) — https://jheusser.github.io/2013/09/08/hawkes.html · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters
- [statement] Garcia Seuma’s in-flight Hyperliquid study reports subcritical branching throughout the studied October 2025 cascade. It limits this result to within-venue feedback and explicitly leaves cross-venue amplification unresolved; subcriticality on one venue is not evidence that the system is safe. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2608.03616 · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters
- [statement] Deduplicate forced liquidation fills by the liquidated-user leg before fitting event intensity. Garcia Seuma warns that the liquidation object appears on both trade legs and otherwise doubles totals. Event-count intensity and forced-notional intensity should consequently be audited as separate measurements. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2608.03616 · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters
- [statement] The evidence here does not validate an endogenous-intensity threshold, directional forecast, or profitable abstention rule for SOL/Jupiter. The branching study states that its severity designs are BTC-centric and its direct in-flight measurement is a single venue/event; the SOL-inclusive recovery study concerns Hyperliquid liquidity recovery. Applying either result to SOL/Jupiter is an untested extrapolation. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2608.03616 · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters · also: https://journals.lincoln.ac.nz/index.php/JFDA/article/view/1395, https://arxiv.org/html/2607.27070
- [statement] Seuma's pre-state branching study finds that the timing signal does not distinguish cascades significantly from trailing-return-matched placebo declines, and its scalar pre-state measures do not grade severity. The author limits the negative result to constructed public-data measures and leaves the accumulated liquidation-threshold map untested. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2608.03616 · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters
- [statement] Seuma limits the measured branching ratio to feedback within one venue. The paper explicitly states that within-venue subcriticality does not preclude system-level amplification. It also warns that products of regime-window means do not identify an instantaneous offspring mean in a non-stationary book. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/html/2608.03616 · keywords: Endogenous liquidation intensity and cascade-risk filters
